output.name: Returned ECOs: users don't know how to rework and resubmit
output.summary: When a reviewer sends an ECO back, often with a comment about affected parts, engineers can't tell what to change or whether to create a new ECO, so they raise a ticket and wait about a day for support to explain the resubmit step.

root_cause.text: Likely the ECO return/rejection step gives users no clear guidance in the tool on what to fix or how to resubmit the same ECO, so every returned ECO becomes a how-to ticket.

quotes.quote: Reviewer sent my ECO back, not sure what to change.
do I need to create a new one?
how do I fix and resubmit?

evidence.text: Every sampled ticket was resolved by explaining the resubmit step and the user resubmitting the same ECO, so no system defect was fixed.

quotes.quote: Explained the resubmit step; user resubmitted the same ECO.
Explained the resubmit step; user resubmitted the same ECO.

evidence.text: Users repeatedly ask whether a returned ECO requires creating a new one, showing the workflow does not make it clear that the existing ECO can be reworked.

quotes.quote: ECO for 450-006537 was returned; do I need to create a new one?
ECO for 330-006273 was returned; do I need to create a new one?

evidence.text: Reviewer return comments frequently concern affected parts, suggesting a common submission error that could be caught before review.

quotes.quote: My ECO came back with a comment about affected parts
My ECO came back with a comment about affected parts

output.fix: Change the ECO return workflow so a returned ECO lands in the originator's task list with the reviewer's required changes shown and a clear 'Revise and resubmit' action on the same ECO. Pair this with a validation check on affected parts at submission so the most common return reason is caught before review.
